short: A long-range strategic bomber that brought the terror of aerial bombardment to British cities.
full:
Entering service in March 1917, the Gotha G.IV was a heavy strategic bomber deployed by the Imperial German Air Service. Capable of carrying a substantial payload over long distances, it was explicitly designed to strike strategic targets well behind enemy lines. Powered by twin Mercedes engines in a pusher configuration, its introduction marked a shift in aerial warfare from localized tactical support to long-range strategic bombing campaigns.

The G.IV is most infamous for executing the first heavier-than-air bombing raids on London in daylight, beginning in the summer of 1917. These attacks caused widespread public panic and forced the British to divert vital fighter squadrons from the Western Front for home defense. Although heavy losses eventually forced the Gothas to switch to night bombing, their operations established the strategic template for the massive bombing offensives of future conflicts before the aircraft was retired at the war's end.
